h1:
Salaya Cafes
9 Work-Friendly Spots With Good Vibes
intro: Salaya's cafe scene has grown right alongside Mahidol University's student crowd. You'll find everything from tiny shops tucked down quiet sois to riverside cafes by the Tha Chin where you can drive out and settle in for the whole day. We picked 9 places locals actually go to, with a clear split between which ones suit long work sessions and which are better for a relaxed photo stop — plus opening hours and rough prices.

blocks.html: If you study or work around Salaya, a cafe is basically a backup office for a lot of people. There are so many shops here it's hard to choose, and each one draws a different crowd. Some are built for quiet, heads-down work with an outlet at every table; others lean into a garden-riverside vibe that's better for chatting than grinding through a deadline. We've ordered them by how suitable they are for working and their overall atmosphere, based on real reviews from people who go often — we haven't personally sat in every one.

items.name: CMD_Salaya
items.blurb: A roast-your-own coffee shop down a Salaya soi, done up in a clean Japanese style with several zones — quiet and spacious. Reviewers rate it as one of the best spots in the area for settling in to work for hours. There are house-baked scones and sourdough to go with the coffee. The catch is limited parking, so you'll be parking along the soi.

items.name: goodwithdude cafe
items.blurb: Inside the Salaya One development near Mahidol, with a minimal Korean look, natural light throughout and strong air-con. There are books and toys you can pick up, so it works whether you come alone or with friends. The signature is the goodwithdude latte paired with a pastry, and prices are student-friendly.
items.meta: Salaya One · roughly 08:30–18:00 (closed some days, check their page first)

items.name: Little Tree Grocery
items.blurb: A tucked-away cafe inside Mahidol's Salaya campus, right by the water. The shop is a timber-frame build surrounded by trees, with both indoor and outdoor seating. The house-baked bagels and cakes are the highlight, and the shaded, cool setting makes it great for reading. Parking on campus is 10 THB per hour (first half hour free).

items.name: Howl Coffee House
items.blurb: An indie-style shop on Soi Salaya 9 with artwork hung around the room and a resident cat that wanders about. The vibe is just right for quiet working or reading, and reviewers like that it never gets too crowded.

items.name: ROLL COFFEE SALAYA
items.blurb: Renovated from an old film-developing warehouse at Kantana Institute, so it carries a studio-loft feel with plenty of photo corners. There's an air-conditioned zone and a shaded outdoor one. The drinks people talk about are the orange coffee and the Dirty Coffee — a good pick for working from late morning into the afternoon.

items.name: The Outsider
items.blurb: A small, warm shop on Soi Salaya 7 across from Mahidol. The standouts are the chewy bread and choux cream, specialty coffee, and the peach tea and matcha. It's a cute, photogenic spot, open Wednesday to Sunday only, with limited parking.

items.name: Mood on Cookies & Coffee
items.blurb: A warm wood-toned cafe beside a canal on the Thawi Watthana–Salaya side. Cookies and coffee are the highlight, with a homey, easy-to-settle-in feel. It opens early, so it's a good stop before work. Closed Thursdays.

items.name: After the Rain Coffee & Gallery
items.blurb: A riverside cafe set in a coconut grove near Thong Khon Thong, close to Mahidol — a very shaded, leafy setting. Buy a drink or food and you get free kayaking. It's better for relaxing and taking photos than long stretches of grinding through work. Mornings have the best views. Closed Mondays.
items.meta: Thong Khon Thong Soi 2 · roughly 08:30–18:00 (closed Mon)

items.name: The Meadow Cafe & Bistro
items.blurb: An open-air cafe and bistro around Sam Phran, with an outdoor zone and a pond. It's pet-friendly and well suited to coming with family or a group of friends. You can work here, but it leans more toward sitting down to eat and chat. Closed Tuesdays.
items.meta: Thong Khon Thong, Sam Phran · roughly 11:00–20:30 (closed Tue)

items.name: Brix House
items.blurb: A white-brick, minimal-style cafe on Phutthamonthon Sai 5 near Makro Salaya. The space is big with plenty of seating zones — reviewers point to the tall window-side tables as a quiet corner to get real work done. The menu runs from coffee and homemade cakes to proper mains like mushroom cream pasta and fish and chips, there is live music on Friday and Saturday evenings, and the front parking lot is genuinely spacious.
items.meta: Phutthamonthon Sai 5 Rd · near Makro Salaya

blocks.title: A tip on parking
blocks.html: The shops down the Salaya sois (CMD, Howl, Outsider) usually have limited parking. If you're coming as a group, it's easier to park inside Mahidol or at Salaya One and walk. The riverside places around Thong Khon Thong have more room to park, but they're farther from central Salaya so you'll need to drive.

blocks.text: Pick a Cafe Based on What You're Doing

blocks.html: Each Salaya cafe suits a different kind of plan, and getting it right from the start saves you a wasted trip. We've split them by the purposes people come for most often.

items.name: Long work or reading sessions
items.blurb: CMD_Salaya, goodwithdude, Howl — quiet, cold air-con and plenty of seating zones, great for grinding through work or revising for exams.

items.name: Photos and relaxing by the water
items.blurb: After the Rain, Little Tree, ROLL — garden and riverside views with lots of photo corners, good for sitting back and chatting.

items.name: With family or dogs
items.blurb: The Meadow and the riverside spots around Sam Phran — open-air, pet-friendly, with room for kids to run around.

items: Student exam season — work-friendly cafes around Salaya fill up fast. If you're planning a long work session, aim to arrive before 10am.
Weekend afternoons — the riverside and photo-spot cafes get busy. If you want good photo corners without waiting, mornings are better.
Each shop's closing day — many close on different weekdays (Outsider opens Wed–Sun, Mood on closes Thursdays, After the Rain closes Mondays), so check the shop's page before you head out every time.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Opening hours and prices for Salaya cafes change often — a lot of these are small shops that adjust their hours by the term. The numbers on this page are rough figures from recent reviews. Before you actually go, double-check the shop's Facebook page or Instagram, especially for the ones that only open on certain days.

faq.q: Which Salaya cafe is best for working?
faq.a: If you're after long, quiet work sessions with plenty of seating zones, CMD_Salaya and goodwithdude are the two reviewers mention most. Howl Coffee House is also nice and quiet and rarely crowded, which makes it good for exam revision.

faq.q: Are there any new cafes opening near Mahidol in Salaya?
faq.a: Salaya sees new shops opening all the time, both inside the Salaya One development (goodwithdude, the Ratchaburi milk shop) and in the sois around Mahidol. Follow local review pages, since small shops open and close quickly — check that a place is still open before you go.

faq.q: Are there any riverside cafes in Salaya?
faq.a: After the Rain Coffee & Gallery sits by the water in a coconut grove around Thong Khon Thong, where buying a drink gets you free kayaking. Little Tree Grocery inside Mahidol is also right by the water, with a shaded, cool setting that's great for relaxing and taking photos.

faq.q: Is there parking at Salaya cafes?
faq.a: Most shops down the Salaya sois have limited parking and you'll be parking along the soi — it's easier to park inside Mahidol or at Salaya One and walk. The riverside places around Thong Khon Thong and Sam Phran have more room to park, but you'll need to drive out to them.

faq.q: Roughly how much does coffee cost at Salaya cafes?
faq.a: Most fall in the range of about 50–120 THB a cup. Shops aimed at students like goodwithdude or the Ratchaburi milk place run a bit cheaper, while specialty roasters and riverside cafes are slightly higher.
